features.text: Patient injured her right ankle while mountain biking, with a twisting motion and a crackling sound.
Patient experiences significant pain on the outer part of her right ankle, rated 8 or 9 on a scale of 1 to 10.
Patient has swelling and bruising on the right ankle.
Patient is unable to bear weight on the right ankle and is limping.
Patient reports instability in the right ankle, feeling it might give way when attempting to bear weight.
Patient experiences numbness in the right foot, especially on the outer side near the ankle, which spreads slightly to the toes.
Patient has no prior history of ankle injuries.
Patient has no prior history of neurological conditions or nerve-related issues.
Patient has no prior history of fractures or bony abnormalities in the ankle.
Patient has no history of undergoing imaging studies such as MRI or ultrasound for this injury.
Patient has no history of undergoing neurological evaluations such as EMG or nerve conduction studies.
Patient has no history of tingling, burning, or weakness in the foot or toes.
Patient has no history of prior ankle injuries or conditions that might affect this current injury.
Patient has been mountain biking for about three years but has not experienced any prior ankle injuries.
Patient has not taken any medications for the injury, as Tylenol did not help.
Patient has no known allergies.
Patient has no known family history of neurological or musculoskeletal conditions mentioned.
Patient has no known social history of smoking or alcohol use mentioned.
X-ray results showed no acute fracture or bony abnormality, only soft tissue injury.
Patient is waiting for the full treatment plan after the X-ray.
